question: to the Commission Özlem Demirel (The Left) Subject:

Since 2015, the German Federal Police has been taking part in EU projects to support the reform of the Tunisian security sector, with a particular focus on developing more efficient police structures and strengthening the coastguard. Supported projects include the construction and extension of facilities in Zarzis, Sfax and Bizerte (2023-2025) and the provision of operational assets (2024). 1.

Which authorities from which Member States and, where applicable, non-EU countries are involved in EU-funded projects to build a maritime training academy for the Tunisian National Guard, what is/was the time frame for these projects, and what are/were the arrangements for funding and delivery?

Which authorities from which Member States and, where applicable, non-EU countries are involved in EU-funded projects to build a maritime rescue coordination centre in Tunisia, what is/was the time frame for these projects, and what are/were the arrangements for funding and delivery?

Does the Commission consider Tunisia to be a safe place pursuant to international law of the sea (i.e. the rules on search and rescue, and those of the International Maritime Organization and the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea) for the disembarkation of rescued persons and, if so, what conflicting observations have been taken into account?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.8.2026) The EU is supporting Tunisia to strengthen its capacities in search and rescue. Enhancing training and operational capacities is essential to save lives at sea and ensure compliance with international standards and procedures. In this context, the EU is working with the International Centre for Migration Policy Development and the German Federal Police to develop training curricula for the Tunisian Coast Guard and support the possible establishment of a maritime training academy. The programme is funded by the EU with EUR 13.5 million and has been implemented since January 2023 for a duration of 42 months. The EU is also cooperating with the French agency Civipol to strengthen the capacities of the Tunisian Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre. The project supports the development of coordination, communication and operational capabilities for maritime search and rescue activities. This activity is funded by the EU with approximately EUR 6.6 million, started in January 2023 and has a duration of 60 months. Search and rescue operations are regulated by international law and aim to ensure that people in distress at sea receive assistance and are disembarked safely and quickly at the closest safe port of disembarkation, in line with international law. The Commission has no competence to coordinate search and rescue operations, nor to indicate safe places for disembarkation, the latter task being the competence of the relevant Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in charge of the coordination of each rescue operation.
